q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
Part III (Articles 12-35) contains Fundamental Rights. Part IV contains Directive Principles.
Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
The 42nd Amendment 1976 added socialist, secular and integrity to the Preamble.
Right to life and personal liberty
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty. Courts have read privacy, health and education into it.

q.hq: अनुच्छेद 21 किस अधिकार की गारंटी देता है?
ho: जीवन एवं व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार
q.he: अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा करता है। न्यायालयों ने इसमें निजता, स्वास्थ्य और शिक्षा को भी शामिल किया है।

q: Dr B. R. Ambedkar called which Article the heart and soul of the Constitution?
Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in:
Part IV (Articles 36-51) contains DPSP. They are not directly enforceable in courts.
Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
The 42nd Amendment 1976 added Fundamental Duties in Part IVA on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right by the:
The 86th Amendment 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free education for children aged 6-14 a fundamental right.
Article 14 of the Constitution deals with:
Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 18 abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.
Which freedom is NOT part of Article 19?
The right to property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment and is now a legal right under Article 300A.
The parliamentary system of government in India is borrowed from:
India adopted the parliamentary system, rule of law and single citizenship from the UK.
Directive Principles were borrowed from the Constitution of:
DPSP was inspired by the Irish Constitution. Fundamental Rights came from the USA.
Fundamental Rights are borrowed from which country?
The Bill of Rights in the US Constitution inspired India's Fundamental Rights.
The Constituent Assembly of India was constituted under the:
The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. It first met on 9 December 1946.
Which Article is described as the soul of the Constitution by some scholars?
Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, is often called the soul of the Constitution because it protects other rights.
Who is the supreme commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
The President is the supreme commander of the armed forces, though actual command rests with the government.
A Money Bill can be introduced only in:
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, with the President's recommendation. The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes.
What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members: 238 representing states and UTs, and 12 nominated by the President.
The current strength of the Lok Sabha is:
The Lok Sabha currently has 543 elected members. The maximum strength is 552 under the Constitution.
The President of India is elected by:
Elected members of Parliament and state legislative assemblies form the electoral college for the President.
Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister of India is appointed by:
The President appoints the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha as Prime Minister.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75.
Who presides over the Lok Sabha?
The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha and decides matters such as Money Bill certification.
Zero Hour in Parliament refers to:
The time immediately after Question Hour
The first hour of the day
The last hour of the day
Zero Hour is the period immediately after Question Hour when members raise urgent matters without prior notice.
Question Hour is a period when:
Question Hour lets members ask questions of ministers and hold the executive accountable.
How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
The President nominates 12 Rajya Sabha members for distinction in literature, science, art and social service.
A no-confidence motion can be moved only in:
A no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha, and if passed, the Council of Ministers must resign.
The President's ordinance-making power is given by:
Article 123 allows the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. They must be approved later.
The minimum age to become President of India is:
A candidate for President must be at least 35 years old and qualified to be a Lok Sabha member.
The Supreme Court of India came into existence on:
The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, two days after the Constitution came into force.
The Supreme Court is established under which Article?
Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court. Article 214 establishes High Courts.
The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
The President appoints the Chief Justice and other judges, traditionally following the collegium's recommendation.
The power of courts to review laws for constitutionality is called:
Judicial review lets courts strike down laws or actions that violate the Constitution.
Which writ means 'to have the body'?
Habeas Corpus orders a person detaining someone to produce them before the court.
The sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is currently:
The Supreme Court has a sanctioned strength of 34 judges, including the Chief Justice, after the 2019 increase.
High Courts are established under which Article?
Article 214 provides for a High Court for each state. Parliament can establish a common High Court for two or more states.
Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman Supreme Court judge in 1989.
Any person to approach court for public interest
PIL allows individuals or organisations to approach courts for issues affecting the public or disadvantaged groups.
Under Article 141, law declared by the Supreme Court is:
Article 141 makes Supreme Court decisions binding on all courts in India.
Supreme Court judges retire at the age of:
Supreme Court judges retire at 65; High Court judges retire at 62.
The collegium system is associated with:
The collegium, led by the Chief Justice, recommends appointments and transfers of judges.
A common High Court can serve:
Parliament can establish a common High Court for two or more states or union territories.
The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 deals with:
Disputes between the Union and states
Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and states or between states.
Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is under:
Under Article 143, the President can refer a question of law or fact to the Supreme Court for advice.
Panchayati Raj institutions were given constitutional status by the:
The 73rd Amendment 1992 added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule, giving constitutional status to rural local bodies.
The three-tier Panchayati Raj system consists of:
Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad
The three tiers are Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti at block level and Zilla Parishad at district level.
All registered voters of the village
The Gram Sabha comprises all registered voters in a village panchayat area and is the base of grassroots democracy.
What proportion of seats in Panchayats is reserved for women?
The Constitution requires at least one-third of seats for women; many states have raised this to 50%.
The normal term of a Panchayat is:
A Panchayat has a five-year term unless dissolved earlier. Elections must be held within six months of dissolution.
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities.
State Finance Commission is constituted under which Article?
Article 243-I provides for a State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats.
The 74th Amendment 1992 gave constitutional status to municipalities and nagar panchayats.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended:
The 1957 Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended democratic decentralisation through a three-tier panchayat system.
The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in:
The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) reviewed Panchayati Raj and recommended a two-tier system.
Which state first implemented Panchayati Raj in 1959?
Rajasthan first implemented Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
The minimum age to contest a Panchayat election is:
A person must be at least 21 years old to contest a Panchayat election.
Reservation of seats in Panchayats for SC and ST is:
Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the area.
The district-level Panchayati Raj body is called:
Zilla Parishad is the district-level body; Panchayat Samiti is at block level and Gram Panchayat at village level.
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 extends the system to Fifth Schedule areas with special powers.
The First Constitutional Amendment was passed in:
The First Amendment 1951 added the Ninth Schedule and imposed reasonable restrictions on free speech.
Which amendment is known as the Mini Constitution?
The 42nd Amendment 1976 made sweeping changes to the Constitution and is called the Mini Constitution.
The right to property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the:
The 44th Amendment 1978 deleted Article 31 and made property a legal right under Article 300A.
The anti-defection law was introduced by which amendment?
The 52nd Amendment 1985 added the Tenth Schedule to curb defections.
The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 by the:
The 61st Amendment 1988 lowered the voting age to 18.
They gave constitutional status to rural and urban local bodies respectively.
The Right to Education was inserted by the:
The 86th Amendment 2002 added Article 21A and amended Article 45 and Fundamental Duties.
The Goods and Services Tax was introduced by the:
The 101st Amendment 2016 introduced GST and created the GST Council.
Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) was provided by the:
The 103rd Amendment 2019 provided 10% reservation for EWS in education and public employment.
Extending SC/ST reservation and ending Anglo-Indian nominated seats
The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures and ended Anglo-Indian nominated seats.
The 106th Amendment 2023, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.
Which amendment made it mandatory for the President to accept the advice of the Council of Ministers?
The 42nd Amendment made ministerial advice binding on the President; the 44th allowed one reconsideration.
The Government of India Act 1935 introduced:
The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy and divided powers into federal, provincial and concurrent lists.
The 39th Amendment was passed during the Emergency to:
Protect the Prime Minister's election from judicial review
The 39th Amendment 1975 placed election disputes involving the President, Vice President, PM and Speaker beyond court scrutiny.
Which amendment added the words 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble?
The 42nd Amendment 1976 added socialist, secular and integrity to the Preamble.
